  Spirit themes wisps, Drowned Archive rising motes, ...); the Nether has embers; the overworld by day has dust that
  spawns only in sunlit air (a CPU march of the heightfield mirror toward the sun) and glints when it's between you and
  the sun. Your breath shows every 3-4 s in first person in the Frost Monastery and wherever it snows. Embers, spores,
  wisps and dust are full bright (Lens's bloom picks them up); frost and breath take the world's light. Gate rates are
  ×1.5 the table's since the L2 tour, and every kind half as big again (they read as specks).
- L2 measured (same vista as L1, p50/p99 ms): off 9.00/13.61, Swift 8.94/14.12, Cinematic 13.13/23.75, Ultra
  16.14/23.66. Ultra holds 60; Cinematic (+4.1 ms) missed 90, so after that tour: the fog glow moved to the quarter-size
  shafts pass, normals from screen derivatives, Cinematic's light buffer 960×540 (24 sun, 6 contact, 8 volume steps),
  Ultra's 1440×810. Measured again in L3's tour.

**L3, water and magic** (looks: `water` 0.6, `heat` 0, `frost` 0, `glow` 0.6 by default; texel 20: r water, g heat,
b frost, a glow; the frame texture's texel 17 x is seconds, wrapping hourly)
- **Water**: the heightfield marks open-water columns (a solid top at the block's base + 0.75, exact in half floats up
  to y 512; the occluder loses nothing). A pixel whose surface lies on such a column's water level (base + 0.889) is
  water; where water draws without depth the pixel shows what's under it, and the reflection sits where the view ray
  crossed the water's surface. Rippling normals (two sines each way, by world position and time), Schlick Fresnel
  (F0 0.02). The reflection: the frame where the reflected ray meets open sky on screen, else the fog's colour; on
  Ultra a 20-step screen-space march of the reflected ray against the depth buffer (nearest first, fading at the
  frame's edge) reflects the scene itself. The sun's glint (pow(R·L, 240) × 5, none in the water's own shade) in the
  light's colour: the reference's glinting river. × `water` and the fog fade. Only where the heightfield is built (an
  overworld sky).
- **Emissive glow**: AWAKEN's glows (bright, saturated, not a warm hue: runes, vortices, the Signal's blue, eyes, the
  gate pillars) bloom up to 2.5× as much as lit surfaces of the same brightness (the prefilter, by `glow`; all tiers),
  and keep their light in Lens 2's shade (the shade's weight × (1 − glowness × `glow`)). They glow through fog
  because the bloom is made before the haze and the fog glow spreads it. No creature was repainted.
- **Heat shimmer** (`heat`: the Nether 0.45, Ember Mines 0.55, Glass Desert 0.4): the frame is read through rippling
  offsets (up to about 0.2% of the screen, more in the lower frame), Cinematic and Ultra only.
- **Frost** (`frost`: Frost Monastery 0.6): frost creeps in from the frame's edges (a band up to 11% of the height ×
  frost, deeper at the corners, crystalline refraction in it and a pale rime with fine streaks over it).
- `glow` 0.9 for the Spirit and Charge themes and the Mirror Palace, 0.8 for the Ember Mines.
- Tour: `tools/autopilot/lens2-l3.txt` (a pool in the lab into the sun, glowing creatures at dusk and night,
  Carillon's river, the Ember Mines' shimmer, the Frost Monastery's frost, the bench).
- L3 measured (with L2's fixes; same vista, p50/p99 ms): off 8.00/12.39 (122 fps), Swift 7.93/11.94, Cinematic
  11.02/16.67 (about 90 fps), Ultra 12.99/19.79 (77 fps): both tiers on budget. The tour harness's `gate interior
  enter` landed in other themes' gates, so heat and frost weren't in its shots.

**L4, volumetric clouds** (Euan, 2026-10-25: "the blocky clouds just aren't it")
- On Cinematic and Ultra Lens draws its own clouds wherever the game would draw clouds (the frame's cloud colour has
  alpha and the player's Clouds setting isn't Off) and the look's `clouds` (cover, default 0.45; 0 keeps the game's) is
  above 0. In `ExtractLevelRenderStateEvent` Lens takes the frame's cloud height and colour and clears that colour's
  alpha, so vanilla's clouds skip that frame; the setting itself is never touched (Swift, Off and a shaderpack keep the
  game's clouds). Rain thickens the cover by up to 0.4. Frame texels 18-19: base height (0: none), cover, the camera's
  x and z plus the wind's drift (0.04 blocks a game tick east) modulo 30720; the cloud colour.
- Shape (`include/lens_clouds.glsl`): a cumulus layer from 6 blocks under the game's cloud height, 84 blocks thick.
  Cover 0.45 leaves most of the sky open between distinct clouds (a coverage threshold of 1 − 0.72 × cover, edges 0.1
  wide), closing into an overcast deck toward 0.95; the threshold rises with height (0.16 × h²), so each cloud narrows
  upward into a dome and only the thickest rise tall (flat 2D cover read as vertical curtains). One tileable noise
  texture, `awaken:lens_cloud_noise` (256×256 RGBA, made in the frequency domain by
  `tools/art/specs/lens_clouds.py`: r coverage, g shape, b billows, a wisps), sampled at 3072, 960, 256 and 120 blocks
  a repeat (all dividing 30720) for where clouds stand and their outlines; their billows are two octaves of a cheap 3D
  value noise in world space (46 and 17 blocks on Ultra, one octave at 38 on Cinematic; flat noise slid with height
  drew vertical streaks), skipped deep inside a cloud. The cover slides up to 45 blocks with height (two noise channels,
  opposite ways; only in the main march, not the light-step and shadow look-ups), so a cloud's sides lean and break
  up instead of standing as straight walls. Flat-ish bases,
  domes that rise where a cloud is thick, billows eating the edges.
- Pass `lens_clouds.fsh` (560×315 on Cinematic, 800×450 on Ultra; then a blit into the persistent
  `awaken:lens_clouds_hist`): each ray marched through the layer (20 / 32 steps, up to 800 / 1100 blocks of it, never
  past nearer terrain), lit by 3 / 5 steps toward the light (doubling from 6 blocks): two octaves of Beer's law (the
  second, at 35% and a quarter of the extinction, stands in for light scattered many times inside, so bases stay soft
  grey-white), σ 0.03 per block, a powder term (thin sunward edges glow, dense cores darken), a phase of 0.85 + 0.9 × HG(0.6) (white from every side, a modest silver
  lining toward the sun; stronger forward lobes blew the sky round the sun out into one white mass), the sun's colour (warm at
  golden hour, the moon's at night) and the sky's light on them (a cool blue with a third of the horizon's colour, by
  the game's cloud colour but never below half and up to 1.95× toward overcast, so a grey sky stays bright grey; 60% at
  the base to 100% at the tops; the sun's light on them × 1.05). Distant cloud melts into the
  fog colour from 1500 blocks and is gone at 5000, so the deck never ends in a line. Accumulated over frames (0.15 /
  0.12 new), reprojected where the ray entered the layer. Out: rgb their light (premultiplied), a
  what shows through.
- The composite lays them over the sky and over anything farther than where the ray enters their layer, before the
  haze. The bloom prefilter (`lens_prefilter_lit.fsh`) folds them into the sky, so bright edges bloom, and the sky's
  alpha (what the screen-space shafts and the sun's halo read) carries 60% of their transmittance: rays break through
  gaps and the halo dims behind a cloud (all of it streaked the whole sky like rain curtains; the shafts also drop to
  0.35 in the composite). The shafts read the open sky's own brightness, not the clouds' (bright cloud tops seen from
  above streaked into rays). The light pass darkens the sun on the land under them (to 28% under thick cloud, along
  the light ray through the layer's middle) and, on Ultra at half strength, in the volumetric beams: moving cloud
  shadows and beams through gaps.
- First tour (bad8a542, 480×270, 20 steps, the first cover curve; p50 ms off 7.74, Swift 7.85, Cinematic 10.73, Ultra
  13.20: the clouds cost no net frame time, since the game's are no longer drawn): too much cover (a stormy deck),
  dark bellies, a hard line toward the horizon, a noise grid; tuned as above.
- Tour: `tools/autopilot/lens2-l4.txt` (Swift's clouds against Lens's: noon, golden hour into the sun, cloud shadows
  over Carillon, above the deck, rain, night; the bench). Final (f53b8bf4, p50 ms): off 6.80, Swift 6.79, Cinematic
  9.96 (100 fps), Ultra 13.46 (74 fps).

**Storm cells** (the Living Wilds' Rolling Storm, 2026-10-26; §21.6): Lens 2 marches each cell in its cloud pass.
- `living.client.StormSky.lensCells` hands Lens up to two cells a frame (as `HoloWorld.lensPlates` does the plates):
  frame texel 20 y their count; texels 42-47, three a cell (`lens_storm_frame.glsl`): centre x, z camera-relative,
  base y, strength; downwind x, z, the ground under it, noise time; the latest flash camera-relative and its strength.
  `LensClient.drawsStormCells()` says whether Lens draws them this frame (Cinematic or Ultra under an overworld sky);
  otherwise the fallback does. Storms draw whether or not the game's clouds are on.
- Shape (`lens_storm.glsl`, §21.6's numbers): cheap cellular puffs (the nearest of 8 jittered points; one octave on
  Cinematic, two on Ultra), the body's wobble, girth and lobes from the cloud noise texture, the anvil's fibres from its
  wisps channel. Light steps (and the land's shadow) keep the big forms only.
- March (`lens_clouds.fsh`): a ray meets a cell in bands, marched in the ray's order, each its own steps by its length:
  rain (ground to base; 18 / 16 blocks a step, at most 10 / 12), body (12 / 10.5, at most 22 / 26), anvil (8 / 7, at
  most 10 / 12), Cinematic / Ultra, so the thin anvil is never stepped over. A turret's surface turns solid within 4
  blocks (9 read as a soft ball at 200 blocks); σ 0.085 a block (a solid mass); 3 light steps (6 blocks, ×2.3); Beer's
  law with a weak multiple-scatter floor (0.22) so the base and the shadowed side go dark; the layer's phase; the sky's
  light as a cool grey-blue of the layer's ambient brightness (its sunset hue turned the shadowed side brown), by height
  from 0.16 at the base (cold and bruised, bluer) to 1 on the tops; rain σ 0.016, its colour that sky light × 0.4 (a
  grey veil, darker than the sky), fading in from 16 to 40 blocks from the camera (nearer, the game's rain falls).
  Lightning lights the cell from within: 3 × exp(-d/55) × exp(-τ) of a cool white from the flash, fading to nothing
  from 130 to 180 blocks (`FLASH_REACH`), where τ is the cloud between the flash and the point (its density at their
  midpoint × d × σ × 0.35, one sample, only while a flash shows), in the cloud and (half) in its rain; with temporal
  Lens a ray that passes within 180 blocks of a flash marches every frame while the flash is over 0.08 (every ray did
  while any flash was above zero: §21.6 "Its cost"), the rest one frame in four; the core round the bolt glows and the cell's shape still
  reads (an even glow over the whole cell blew a night strike out to a white disc); while a flash shows, the pixel takes up to 85% of this
  frame instead of 12-15%, so it lights at once and fades as an afterglow. The layer's clouds thin to nothing within
  330-450 blocks of a cell (it clears the sky round it), so the layer's march can skip the cell's bounds without a cut.
  History reprojects where the ray first met cloud (was: where it entered the layer). A ray that met none looks up
  `historyDepth` (`lens_clouds.fsh`): where cloud would be on it (the layer's entry, `stormGuess`: tight cylinders round
  the body, shelf, anvil plate and rain core), or the terrain's own point when nearer. Never a block ahead (what a miss
  took before 2026-10-27: its parallax carried the history across the screen as the camera moved) and never the cell's
  bounding volume (hundreds of blocks in front of its surface: the storm swam against the world as you walked; Euan's
  report 2026-10-27, "the storm goes crazy while I move").
- The composite lays the cloud buffer over anything farther than where the ray enters a cell's bounds (320 radius
  round 60 downwind of its centre, ground to 48 over the top; the anvil band 245 round 150 downwind, from 72 under
  the top), never nearer than 16 blocks; the light pass darkens the
  sun on the land under a cell, sampled where the light ray crosses three heights of its outline (`stormOutline`: body,
  shelf, flanking towers and anvil with soft edges, no noise and no texture; long shadows at dusk).
  Its bright, flashing edges bloom and cut the screen-space shafts like the layer's clouds.
- It builds from its base up (the density cut at a height rising with its strength, softened over 40 blocks) and rains
  out from the top down, as the fallback's cells do; its rain starts once the base has formed (strength 0.1-0.4).
- Lens dims its sun by the world's own weather, not the storm's local rain (`StormSky.serverRain/serverThunder`): the
  sun still lights its towers and the land beside it, and the cell's own shadow darkens the land under it.
- **Wet surfaces** (Cinematic, Ultra; any rain, the storm's local rain included): in the composite, a surface open to the
  sky in its column (the heightfield's top with leaves; under leaves 40%) gets wet by the rain level: 16% darker, 10%
  richer, and what faces up a dull sheen of the haze colour at glancing angles (Schlick-like, power 4, × 0.22).

**Holo world plates** (the Living Wilds' creature plates, 2026-10-25): plates write their depth at a creature's
distance (4-40 blocks), beyond the 1.25-block rule that keeps the panels and the hand out. `HoloWorld.lensPlates`
hands Lens the plates drawn this frame (up to 6: centre, half-width and half-height vectors, camera-relative); the frame
texture carries them (texel 20 x the count, texels 24-41, three a plate; it grew to 48×1), and a surface point within
0.15 block of a plate's plane and inside its rectangle (`onPlate` in lens_frame.glsl) gets no shadow, AO, key or shade
and no haze. With the K panel open they dim with the rest of the world (the focus dim stays).

**Lens on Apple** (orchestrator brief 2026-10-26 from Euan's "maybe there's a way to massively improve them to really
optimise for macOS"; docs/perf/LENS-APPLE.md):
- **Measured** (Roost at noon; MacBook at Euan's 4.7 MP world; GPU world pass). Swift costs nothing over Lens off. The
  lit composite was ~4 ms of Cinematic's ~3.6 over Swift, everything else under 0.6 ms a pass. Inside the composite:
  - its light, 1.15 ms;
  - the cloud blend, 0.45 ms;
  - the scatter, 0.5 ms.
  A pass of one texture sample costing 0.45 ms pointed at its ~70 per-pixel fetches of values every pixel shares.
- **Tiles** (Turbo, `dev.awaken.turbo.tiles`, `awaken.tiles.mixins.json`, setting `lensTiles`, default on;
  autopilot `lens tiles`). Vanilla gives every post chain target a full-size D32 depth buffer, clears colour and depth
  each frame in a pass of their own, and opens every pass LOAD/STORE on both; on a tile-based GPU each is a trip
  through memory for the whole target. For `awaken:lens_*` chains only:
  - per-frame targets have no depth and no clear pass;
  - histories have no depth (their clear when made stays);
  - passes open CLEAR with no depth attached.
  Every Lens pass is a full-screen triangle with no blend or discard, and no post pipeline tests depth, so the picture
  is the same (look tour lens-apple-look). It is version-locked, logs a probe line, and is off on failure.
- **The uniform block** (`LensBlock`: LensF[48], LensP[32], LensUse; include lens_block.glsl, tools/lens/block.py;
  autopilot `lens block`):
  - The Lens chains declare it with zeros on every pass whose shader reads F() or P().
  - Lens writes the same values to a live buffer each frame (the parameters as byte/255, what the texture fetch
    returns), and Tiles' PostPass hook binds it.
  - With LensUse.x at 0 (not bound), F() and P() read the textures as before.
- **Together, measured** (GPU world pass, old path → new; frame p50):

  | Look | GPU world pass | frame p50 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Swift | 7.71 → 7.13-7.20 ms | 9.59 → 9.1 ms (105 → 111 fps) |
  | Cinematic | 11.51 → 10.06 ms | 13.26 → 11.8 ms (75 → 85 fps) |
  | Ultra | 13.33 → 11.8 ms | 15.04 → 13.65 ms (66 → 73 fps) |

  The look is unchanged. The composite's volumetric term also reuses the light buffer's upsample (identical output).
- **Measurement tools (dev only):**
  - probe chains `awaken:lens_probe_<tier>_<group>` (tools/lens/probes.py: one pass group swapped for lens_null);
  - composite sub-probes (lens_composite_probe_<part>.fsh, PROBE_NO_* defines);
  - autopilot `lens chain <name>|off`.

**Temporal clouds and light** (Euan, 2026-10-26: "Start all three ideas now", docs/perf/IDEAS-26OCT.md B; setting
`lensTemporal`, default on; autopilot `lens temporal on|off|setting`):
- Why: at the Roost, Lens Cinematic cost ~5.4 ms of a ~21 ms frame (docs/perf/PERF-26OCT.md). Its marches (the clouds
  at 560×315 / 800×450, the light buffer at 960×540 / 1440×810) already blend into a reprojected history, but every
  pixel marched every frame.
- The clouds: a pixel marches one frame in four, a 2×2 pattern of 8×8-pixel tiles turning with the frame counter
  (frame texel 12 w). Whole tiles, so the GPU's SIMD groups skip together: the first, per-pixel pattern left a marching
  pixel in every group and saved nothing (Cinematic 13.22 ms off, 13.25 on).
  - On the other three frames it keeps last frame's clouds, reprojected to where cloud would be on its ray (`historyDepth`:
    the layer's entry or a storm's body, the terrain's point when nearer; 150 blocks when the camera is inside the layer).
  - A march blends in at 1 - (1 - f)^4 of the old weight f, so the clouds answer over time as before.
  - It marches anyway with no history (a cut, a teleport, a long gap), off screen, or while lightning flashes.
- The light buffer (sun visibility, contact shadows, AO, volumetric light): a checkerboard of 8×8 tiles marches each
  frame, alternating.
  - On its off frame a pixel keeps its reprojected history where at least 0.4 of the 2×2 taps saw the same distance.
  - A new surface (disocclusion) marches.
  - A march blends in at 1 - (1 - f)^2.
- Frame texel 17 y carries the switch; with it off, both passes are exactly as before.
- Measured (perf tour `tools/autopilot/lens-temporal-perf.txt`, 26 Oct; MacBook at Euan's 4.7 MP world, the Roost,
  noon, a quiet machine; GPU world pass p50):

  | | off | on |
  |---|---|---|
  | Ultra | 17.02 ms | **15.12 ms** (frame p50 19.4 → 17.3, 51 → 58 fps) |
  | Cinematic (paired windows) | 13.95, 13.53 ms | 13.70, 13.13 ms (−0.25 to −0.4) |

  - Lens Swift is 9.29 ms, so the whole of Lens Cinematic is ~4.2 ms over Swift and the marches are a small part of
    it. The rest is the full-size passes; time them per pass next.
  - Look tour `tools/autopilot/lens-temporal-look.txt` (CI): no smear and no tile blocks, at rest or in a 180° turn.

## 23. Creature life (Fresh Animations in the pack, and a life layer on every body of ours; Euan 2026-10-25)

Euan: every mob, ours included, "still feels a bit rigid and static". Approved: "Both: Fresh Animations + our life layer".

**Vanilla bodies: Fresh Animations.** The pack's `feel` profile adds Entity Model Features 3.3.12, Entity Texture
Features 7.2.6 and the Fresh Animations resource pack 1.11.1 (`tools/pack.py` now locks Modrinth resource packs like
mods, under the `minecraft` loader; `install` puts them in `resourcepacks/` and appends them to options.txt's
`resourcePacks` only if missing, never touching the player's own packs; `remove` switches off and deletes only what it
put there; `export` ships them under `resourcepacks/`). EMF finds models by the vanilla layer a renderer bakes, so our
gate monsters on vanilla bodies (zombie, wolf, hoglin, iron golem...) animate the Fresh Animations way too, which is
wanted: Fresh Animations keeps the vanilla UV layout (it only adds a few eyelid pixels), so our skin layer still fits.
Our own bodies live on `awaken:` layers with no .jem, so EMF leaves them alone; they get the life layer instead.

**Our bodies: the life layer** (`mobs/client/life`). One procedural layer on every model of ours (hero rigs, P3 rigs,
the 14 hand-built bodies), driven by bone names and a temperament, never by per-creature code:
- **Bones by name** (`LifeBones`, plain data): head, neck, jaw, eyes, lids, body/chest (breath), and the springy roles:
  ears (also tufts, crests, plumes, sails), antennae (whiskers, palps, a lure's rod), tails (flukes, streamers, fans),
  dangling parts (manes, beards, ruffs, skirts, tentacles, reeds, brambles, lamps, a bell's clapper), wings, fins and
  gills, arms (only where the temperament swings them: lords, spirits, the Mycelord, the Hushling, the Breathbell). A
  part named only "tip" or "end" takes its parent's role; links of one role chain (follow-through down a tail).
- **Temperaments** (`assets/awaken/life/creatures.json`, schemaVersion 1): cute, grazer, hunter, beast, lord, monster,
  spirit, insect, swimmer, citizen; from the fauna role (ambient cute, neutral grazer, hunter, beast) or the tier (gate
  monsters monster, wardens beast, lords and guardians lord, nightmares spirit), and per-creature entries on top. Fields:
  breath (Hz) and depth, blink interval (0 = never: insects, fish, serpents, spiders, the eyeless and the faceless), head
  speed and damping, eye lead, spring Hz, damping and gain, step bob (px), sway (deg), turn lean, fidget interval and
  weights, arms, stagger, mass. Cute creatures are quick and bouncy (head 14 rad/s, underdamped, springs 3.4 Hz), hunters
  smooth and still (critically damped, blink every 5-11 s), beasts slow and heavy (head 3.6, springs 1.4 Hz, bob 1.3 px).
- **Per creature, per frame** (`Life`, made once, nothing allocated after): motion from the render state (velocity and
  acceleration in model space, yaw rate); breathing (a quicker in-breath, faster and deeper after running or a blow,
  decaying over ~9 s; on hero rigs it also speeds up the creature's own idle clip); blinks (0.16 s, 15% double); the head
  follows its target on a damped spring (the AI's look, an idle's glance, a lead into a turn) and eye bones take the
  rest (eyes first); springs integrated at up to 120 Hz substeps from the body's acceleration, the parent bone's clip
  motion (a head toss swings the ears), the yaw, a blow and a fall, swing only (no twist), capped per role; the step's
  dip (twice a stride, from the gait clip's own stride length) and weight sway; a lean into turns.
- **Idle fidgets**, only when still, calm and within 32 blocks, chosen by weight from what the body has: look around (the
  head lags the eyes), sniff (head down, quick nods), flick (an ear, a tail, a feeler or a wing), shake (body roll at
  7.5 Hz, everything loose flops; a creature fresh out of water shakes itself dry once it stops), stretch, yawn (eyes
  squint shut), scratch (a hind leg kicks), perk (head up, alert), settle (a weight shift), graze (a walker on planted
  feet only: 5-9 s; the forequarters dip 0.07 rad and sink 0.8 px, the neck bends 0.65 rad and sinks 3 px in front of the
  chest (the head 0.55 rad without a neck), the head looks 0.55 rad down and drifts side to side, a tug and a jaw snap
  at each bite (1.4 a second for a cow's 14 px legs, quicker for shorter legs, up to 3.2: a chicken pecks), then 1.6 s
  head up chewing; the grazer temperament weighs it 6, the beast 3; Euan 2026-10-29). A fidget it walks out of is
  over once it has faded (a pause later in the walk dropped the second close tour's sheep back into the middle of a
  graze). Herds never move in step:
  each creature's timers, breath phase and rate (±10%) and idle clock start from its own seed.
- **Graph blending, no pops**: the angry stance, held poses, swimming and the glide ease in and out (0.05-0.3 s); swim
  and wing loops run on integrated clocks (age × speed jumped their phase when the speed changed); one-shot clips (bite,
  flinch, strike, roar, warning) hold their last frame and let go over 0.2 s; the fall crossfades from the live pose over
  0.25 s; a swimmer's pitch eases out of the water.
- **Hero clips on top** (named beasts, Gate Lords): a wind-up gathers the body low (0.7 px) and trembles at 17 Hz as it
  nears the strike (tension², the tell); a roar opens with a full chest and shudders through the head and every loose
  part, and bodies without a roar clip rear back (a Gate Lord turning on you: vanilla's aggressive flag); a blow knocks
  the body away from the camera and it sways back on its weight (a damped spring kicked once: heavy beasts reel less and
  slower); the fall: the eyes close at 55% of it, one last breath, and when the body lands (85% of the death clip's drop,
  `LifeRig.landing`) a thud: one bounce and every mane, ear and bramble flops. Bodies without a death clip (the hand-built
  ones, every boss on a vanilla body: lords, guardians, sovereigns, the Shadow, wardens) topple instead of vanilla's
  flip: a stagger back, an accelerating fall (90° by 0.7 s), one bounce, settled by 0.95 s, inside vanilla's 20 ticks.
- **Blinking**: eyelid bones close the way the rig's own clips close them (the Mire Mother, the Seated One); eye bones
  squash (the snails' stalks, the Lantern Maw); otherwise the closed-eye skin: `tools/art` records every pixel painted
  inside `with P.eyes():` (`fauna_rig.EyeRec`) and writes `<id>_blink.png` (the skin under the eye with a lash line)
  and `<id>_glow_blink.png` (the eyes' light out); the renderer draws them while the eyes are shut. 14 creatures have
  them; existing textures are byte-identical.
- **The look reaches the model** (fixed 2026-10-29): NeoForge clears a render state's data right after
  `extractRenderState` (`RenderStateExtensions.onUpdateEntityRenderState`), so the `AwLook` our renderers set there was
  gone by `setupAnim`: `Life.from` was null and the layer's pose (legs, flight, springs, blinks), tint, glow and flash
  never drew on the Hero, Wild and hand-built (`AwMobRenderer`) bodies; only form bodies (extracted from a modifier)
  had it. `MobsClient` registers a render state modifier that puts the entity's same look back after the clear. Bosses
  (the kit's renderer, and `AwMobRenderer`'s boss tiers) are left out until the boss work takes it.
- **Cost and limits**: client only; nothing allocated per frame (render states carry a reference); springs and fidgets
  off past 32 blocks (springs settle), blinks off past 32; breath and the slow head everywhere (cheap). Reduced motion
  (`awaken-client` `reducedMotion`, the body module's) turns idle fidgets off and halves springs, tremble and stagger;
  breathing and blinking stay.
- **Other modules' bodies** use `CreatureLife` (§12). Carillon wires its citizens itself (M4 B3): temperament `citizen`
  (no step bob or sway, gentle springs, look and settle fidgets), `lookWeight` for "only look at the player up close or
  at whoever they talk to", clips win where they drive a bone (applied after the layer).
- **Not here**: the Ritual of the Bell's cast (its model plays exactly the clip its stage asks for); humanoid gate
  monsters on vanilla bodies (Fresh Animations' job, plus the boss topple and stagger above).
- Test: `creature_life_binds` (every body of ours gets a temperament, every rig and hand-built naming with ears or a tail
  gets springs on them, every creature that blinks has lids, eye bones or a closed-eye skin). Tour:
  `tools/autopilot/creature-life.txt` (PACK=perf,feel; clips in run-autopilot/clips/life_*).

### 23.1 Motion: feet on the ground, weight over them (Euan 2026-10-29: "on par with Fresh Animations")

Every Awaken creature on our own bodies (not bosses, not people) moves to the bar Fresh Animations sets for vanilla's
mobs. The principles are learned from it, never its files: a stride driven by ground speed, weight that shifts over the
feet, overlap and follow-through, idles with variety, head and eye life, reactions to hits and turns, anticipation and
follow-through on attacks, and every creature moving the way its body and nature say. The life layer above already gives
breath, springs, fidgets, the look, the stagger and the fall; the motion layer adds the feet and the carriage.

- **Data**: `assets/awaken/life/motion.json` (schemaVersion 1), by rig id. A body not listed moves exactly as before (the
  kit's bosses have no entry). `gait`: `pattern` (`ripple`: one pair at a time from the back forward, each `lag` of a
  cycle after the pair behind it, the two sides half a cycle apart (`lag` 0: one wave over the side); `alternate`:
  opposite sets; `ripple-alternate`: the first walking, the second once it runs, 0.45 in and 0.25 out), `duty` (share of
  a cycle a foot stands, walking and running), `lift` (px a step rises), `stride` (blocks a cycle covers; 0 the rig's
  own), `reach` (blocks a planted foot may trail before it steps at once), `settle` (blocks from home a foot may rest
  when the body stops), `crouch` (px the body sinks on its legs), `radius` and `fan` (where each foot stands: px out
  from its hip, the front ones fanned forward and the back ones back by `fan` degrees), `regrip` (seconds between a calm
  creature's idle re-grips of one foot), `swing` (the longest a step takes), `bob` (px the body sinks while feet are up),
  `roll` (radians it leans off a lifted foot; a four-legged body's hind foot counts 0.6, so a trot's diagonal pair
  still tips it off the forefoot), `rock` (radians it noses down while forefeet are up and up while hind feet are,
  twice a stride on a walk), `rear` (how far the front `rearPairs` pairs, 1 unless set, let go to the
  clips while the body rears: a wind-up, a strike or a cue, a roar, or a still threat; a roar lets one pair more go),
  `knees` (`auto`, `forward`, `back`: which way a leg that stands straight at rest bends; `auto` breaks the forelegs of a
  body with legs one behind another forward and every other leg back, a bird's and a biped's back; a leg bent at rest
  keeps its own bulge).
  `body`: `headLevel` (the head holds level against the gait's and the ground's pitch and roll), `twist` (the body turns
  this share of its look, at most 0.35 rad), `slope` (it pitches and rolls with the ground under its planted feet),
  `land` (a landing squashes it by how far it fell: a spring at 3 Hz kicked by the fall speed), `still` (a stalking
  hunter holds its breath to a quarter, plays no fidgets and no re-grips), `creep` (px it sinks while stalking), `shift`
  (px its weight drifts over its planted feet while it stands, on two slow unrelated beats in its own phase, leaning a
  little over the side it moves to; the legs give and take under it; gone in 0.6 s once it walks, stalks or lets go),
  `nod` (radians the neck, or the head without one, dips while a forefoot is up: a grazer's head bobbing with its steps).
- **Legs** (`LegRig`, plain data, checked on the server): a leg is a LEG-role bone that hangs from a non-leg with exactly
  one LEG-role child (hip and knee), which has at most one LEG-role child of its own (a foot, the tarsus of a long
  spider leg: it rides the shin as it stands at rest, the IK reaching with its tip) and nothing below that. Each is posed
  by two-bone IK in the hip's parent frame: the
  knee goes where the two lengths meet on the side it bulged at rest (its pole), the hip's rest frame is turned onto the
  new thigh frame, and the knee only bends about its own hinge (the shortest turn between two directions both square to
  it). Applied last in `LifeRig.apply` (after the clips, the look and the springs), blended over the clips by the feet's
  weight; out of reach the leg points straight at its target. Only bodies whose body bone carries the head (the feet
  ride the body bone; a pose-stack body would carry them off their spots), or that have no head bone at all and a motion
  profile (the weaver queen's face is on its thorax; a headless body without one keeps its old pose-stack motion).
- **Rigid legs** (`knees: rigid`; Euan 2026-10-29, the form cow's shins came off its thighs): a blocky leg whose shin
  pivots right on the thigh's end face opens a wedge at any knee bend, so it has no knee, as Fresh Animations' cows,
  pigs, sheep, chickens and horses have none. Its knee holds its rest whatever the clips do; the whole leg turns toward
  its foot's spot about a point `shoulder` × its length above the hip (a shoulder blade's or a pelvis's swing: the
  leg's top slides fore and aft inside the body, as far as the body's own cubes have room ahead of and behind it, so
  the leg reaches far at a modest angle), then its pivot slides straight up into the body (at most half the leg) or a
  touch down (the depth the leg's top sits inside the body, less 1 px for its tilted corners) until the foot stands on
  its spot. The vault reaches from that turned pivot. The check: every leg straight at rest whose thigh doesn't reach
  past the knee's pivot by enough to hide 20° of bend (the thigh's overreach against the shin's half-thickness) must be
  rigid. Rigid: the forms' pigs, cows, sheep (shoulder 0.5) and chickens (0), the sow, the stag and the ram (0.5);
  their steps lift 0.65 of what the knees had (the leg slides up into the body to clear the ground), and a rigid hoof's
  swing runs a touch past its spot and settles back onto it (its path's ease plus 0.25·u·sin(πu), about 4%).
- **Fresh Animations' walk, read close up** (2026-10-29, `mob-anims-close`: vanilla's cow, pig, sheep beside ours side
  on): their forefoot steps before the hind foot on its side (ours stepped hind first, so the near feet met in a V under
  the belly), their legs reach forward more than they trail, and the cow and sheep step shorter. So the four-legged
  walkers (the form grazers, the sow, the stag, the ram) ripple from the front (`lag` -0.25), land 0.2 of a stand
  further ahead (`lead`), roll 0.045 off a lifted foot (a trot's diagonal pair too), rock 0.035 fore and aft, hold the
  head 0.7 level, and the forms' cows and sheep walk 0.8 of their old stride.
- **Starts** (2026-10-29, the second close tour: our cow, pig and spider did the splits setting off and breaking into
  a trot, and FA's never do, its swing growing with the pace): from a stand, or into a new gait, the stride starts at
  0.4 of its length and grows to the whole of it over 0.9 s (a change of gait starts at 0.7), so the first steps are
  short and quick and the feet still waiting their turn are never left far behind. A landing is never further ahead of
  its home than its place in a steady stride (duty × stride × (0.5 + lead), plus 5% of a stride), and a planted foot
  trailing more than its steady lift point (duty × stride × (0.5 - lead)) plus 30% of a stride steps at once (a
  catch-up, 0.75 of a swing, 0.12 s to `swing`; past 38% it steps even while a neighbour is up).
- **Turns** (2026-10-29, the orchestrator's read of the close tour: a cow and a pig turned on the spot crossed their
  legs in an X and were still leaning a second and a half later): a planted foot's trail is read along its own home's
  path, the body's turn included (its home 0.1 s on, from the body's way and turn), and the landing's cap counts the
  turn's speed at the feet too. Swinging round on the spot (the turn's speed at the feet over the body's way), a foot
  steps as soon as it is three `settle`s off its spot and slides after the body past four (FA's feet slide through a
  turn; a quick one outruns any steps). A rigid leg's planted foot slides rather than lean more than 40° from its
  shoulder (`Legs.SLIP`). Standing, feet off their spots step back the furthest first, up to half of them at once but
  never two neighbours (one at a time left the last leg leaning for 1.5 s). The feet stand and step under the body
  bone's twist toward its look (`Legs.face`; vanilla keeps a standing mob's body 50° behind its facing after a turn,
  so the head stays round and the twist stays), though they are handed to the legs in the root's model space.
- **Feet** (`Legs`, per creature, from the render extraction once a frame; nothing allocated): a planted foot keeps its
  world position while the body moves over it. A gait clock runs with the ground covered plus the arc the feet sweep
  when it turns on the spot (yaw × the feet's mean distance from the middle), so a turn steps too. A foot lifts when the
  clock reaches its place in the pattern, swings for (1 - duty) of a cycle (0.08 s to `swing`) on an arc that peaks
  before the middle, and lands where its home will be halfway through its next stand (velocity and turn rate ahead,
  capped at 80% of `reach`), on the ground under that spot (collision tops from a block above the feet to three below,
  never more than a block up or down). A foot left beyond `reach` steps at once unless a neighbour (same side, next
  rank, or its opposite) is up. Stopped for 0.3 s, the foot furthest out of place (beyond `settle`) steps back under the
  body, one at a time; a calm one re-grips. The body rides its feet: half the planted feet's mean height (±4 px), nose
  up a rise and leaning across a slope (front against back feet, left against right, ±0.35 rad, eased over 0.12 s),
  sinking `bob` × the share of feet in the air and leaning off a lifted one. The hips vault: a straight leg at full
  height reaches only a little forward or back, so the body drops as far as its furthest planted foot needs (past what
  the crouch and the ground sink it, at most a quarter of the mean leg, eased over 0.05 s), which gives a long-legged
  walk its dip at every step. Off the ground (the `P_AIR` pose bit),
  hanging, resting, sleeping, beached, deflated, swimming or dying, the clips own the legs (the weight eases out over
  0.12 s, the feet held planted meanwhile); landing, the feet stand at home again and ease back in over 0.15 s. A
  first sight or a jump of more than 3 blocks stands them at home. Inputs from the renderer: `grounded` (the feet may
  plant), `legsFree` (a pose that holds the legs), `stalking`, `rearing` (a held pose that rears it on its hind feet: the
  front pairs go to the clip), `gaitRun` (0..1) and `bodyScale` (a renderer's own scale on top of the entity's, so the
  feet's world spots match the drawn body: the cave spider's 0.7). WildRenderer: grounded unless `P_AIR`, legs free while
  hanging, resting, beached, asleep or deflated, rearing while it ripens. HeroRenderer (the named beasts): grounded unless
  `P_AIR`, legs free while it rests or burrows. FormRenderer: on the ground and not climbing.
- **Clips** of a profiled body move the body over its feet, the head, the tail, the jaw, and own the legs only when the
  feet let go (hanging, leaping, dying, a wind-up's front pair). Their walk and run legs stay for anything drawn without
  a life (the clip is what shows if nothing plants the feet).
- **Drip Lurker** (`drip_lurker`; six two-bone legs, hunter): ripple-alternate, duty 0.78/0.55, steps 3/4.5 px high, feet
  10 px out from the hips fanned 42°, crouch 1 px, reach 0.55, re-grips every 3-8 s, `rear` 0.9; head level 0.6, twist
  0.2, slope 0.8, land 1, `still` with a 2.5 px creep; temperament: no step bob, sway 0.3, look/sniff/stretch/settle
  fidgets. It strides 1.0 blocks walking and 1.3 running (its rig's 1.0/1.8; were 1.6/3.0, too long for its legs). Motion: it waits on
  planted feet with the cone swaying like a stalactite in a draught and the fangs tasting the air one at a time; it
  creeps low on a slow ripple of single steps, holding its breath and its fidgets while it stalks; it glides level over
  its feet when it walks (no bob), cone lagging, and leans into a run on alternating sets; angry and still it sinks, head
  down, fangs spread and quivering; every wind-up lets its front pair go so it rears them, spread and trembling, before
  the lunge throws the body forward with the fangs snapping shut, overshoots and settles; Spike Drop rears high then
  crashes cone-first, the body squashing and the cone whipping after; a blow jerks the body up and back over its planted
  feet with the cone lagging; it dies rearing with its legs flung out, drops on its side and the legs curl up over it
  and twitch one by one; hanging, each leg flexes on its own breath round the cone. Its rest pose stands the front pair
  forward and the back pair back (the rig had the front legs raked backward).
- **Wickling** (`wickling`; four two-bone legs): a salamander's diagonal trot (`alternate`) at every speed on tiny quick
  steps (1/1.6 px high, stride 0.35/0.6 blocks, 0.15 s swings, reach 0.18), its spine wave from the clip bending over the
  planted feet, a lizard's roll (0.04); head level 0.4, twist 0.4, shift 0.25. Ripening it rears on its hind feet and its
  forefeet, drawn up off the ground, knead the air in turn while the tail braces.
- **Hushling** (`hushling`; two two-bone hind legs, long arms swung by its clips): a crouched biped's alternating steps,
  duty 0.6/0.4, 2/3.5 px, stride 0.9/1.5 blocks; its body rises (bob -0.6) while a foot is up, as a biped's does, and
  rolls off it (0.05); a hunter: `still`, creep 1.5; head level 0.5, twist 0.3, shift 0.5.
- **Weaver Queen** (`weaver_queen`, named beast; eight three-bone legs, femur 12, tibia 14, tarsus 6 px, no head bone):
  an alternating tetrapod on long reaching steps (4/7 px high, stride 1.4/2.6 blocks, reach 0.9, 0.32 s swings), bob 0.5;
  twist 0.15, slope 0.85, shift 0.9 (the heaviest drift: a big body settling over eight feet).
- **Form spiders** (`form_spider_2`..`_5`, the forms' C-and-up bodies, SPEC 21.13; eight two-bone legs, coxa fan then
  femur and shin): they replace the spider Fresh Animations draws below C, so they must beat it. Alternating tetrapods
  (L1 R2 L3 R4, then the others) on their rest stance, duty 0.62/0.5, steps from 3/5 px (C) to 4.5/7 px (S) high, reach
  0.5 to 0.7 blocks, quick swings (0.22 to 0.28 s), bob 0.35 to 0.5 px, `rear` 1 (angry, its front pair spread off the
  ground; a roar, both front pairs); head level 0.5, twist 0.25, slope 0.85, land 1. The renderer plants the feet while it
  stands on the ground and not on a wall (`onGround` and not climbing); the cave spider's body is 0.7 of the spider's.
- **Thousandfoot** (`thousandfoot`, named beast; fourteen two-bone legs, seven segments): a centipede's ripple, back to
  front with each pair a fifth of a cycle behind (two waves down each side), the sides in opposition; duty 0.65/0.55,
  steps 2.5/3.5 px, stride 1.0/1.6 blocks (its clips' 2.6/5.0 are far past its legs' reach), reach 0.5, quick 0.22 s
  swings, almost no bob (0.1 px) or roll; its walk's sideways spine wave bends the segments over the planted feet; a wind-up
  lets its front three pairs go (`rearPairs` 3: the Coil Strike's S rears them), a roar four. Head level 0.3, twist 0.3,
  slope 0.7, land 0.8. Its rest pose sits a pixel lower with the legs out flatter (thigh -10°, shin 84°) so every foot
  reaches the ground (they hung 3 px above it).
- **Form grazers** (`form_pig_2`..`_5`, `form_cow_2`..`_5`, `form_sheep_2`..`_5`, SPEC 21.13; four straight two-bone
  legs, thigh and shin): a lateral walk (`ripple-alternate`: right hind, right fore, left hind, left fore, a quarter of a
  cycle apart) into a trot of diagonal pairs; they stand sunk 2.2-2.5% of a leg on their crouch so the forelegs'
  knees break forward and the hocks back (about 25° at rest, deep while a foot is up), and the neck nods with the
  forefeet (`nod`). Strides come from the leg (L px): a planted foot sweeps ±0.45 L walking and ±0.5 L running, so
  stride = 0.45 L / (8 × duty) walking and 0.5 L / (8 × duty) running (a pig's 0.66/1.19 blocks at rung 2 to a cow's
  1.56/2.78 at 5; the rigs' clip strides were past their legs). Pig: duty 0.68/0.42, steps a fifth of a leg high (a third running), quick 0.22 s swings, bob 0.35,
  roll 0.035, nod 0.07, shift 0.35-0.5. Cow: duty 0.72/0.45, steps 17%/28% of a leg, 0.3 s swings, bob 0.5, nod 0.09,
  shift 0.6-0.9 (a heavy body settling). Sheep between them, nod 0.08. All `rear` 1: angry and still, its front pair
  goes to the clip so it paws; a charge's wind-up rocks back on planted hind feet. Head level 0.3-0.35, twist 0.2-0.25,
  slope 0.8-0.85.
- **Form chickens** (`form_chicken_2`..`_5`; two straight legs from the base, the foot drawn on the shank): a bird's
  alternating strut, duty 0.62/0.4, stride from the leg as the grazers', steps 28%/40% of a leg high, quick 0.16 s swings, sunk 5% of a leg so the ankles
  break back; the head holds still in space against the body (head level 0.7) while the clip thrusts the neck; bob
  0.4, roll 0.05, land 1.2, shift 0.2.
- **Hoofed beasts** (named beasts on four two-bone legs, by HeroRenderer; strides from the foreleg as the grazers'):
  the **Briar Sow** (`briar_sow`; short forelegs, 10 px, under a heavy chest, long bent hind legs) walks a lateral
  sequence on short quick steps (0.8/1.49 blocks, 2/3.5 px high, 0.26 s swings) into a trot when she charges, sunk
  0.3 px, bob 0.4, nod 0.06, a heavy drift (shift 0.7), land 1.2; the **Old Antler** (`old_antler`; 18 px legs) a
  stag's high-stepping walk (1.41/2.81 blocks, 3.5/6.5 px high, 0.32 s swings, reach 0.7), the head carried high
  (head level 0.45, nod 0.05); the **Stonehorn** (`stonehorn`; 12 px legs) a ram's sure-footed walk (0.96/1.79 blocks,
  2.5/4.5 px) that pitches and rolls with the rock under it (slope 0.9), nod 0.07, shift 0.8. All `rear` 1: a still
  threat or a wind-up hands the front pair to the clip (the sow's snort and paw, the ram's stamp).
- **Flight** (`Flight`, plain math checked on the server; a `fly` block, by rig id or, for a hand-built body, by its
  creature id): while airborne or swimming (or `always`, for a body always under way: serpents, the ray) the body noses
  into a cruise (`tilt` at `fast` blocks a second) and pitches along its path's climb or dive (`climb`, the share), banks
  into a turn (`bank`, radians per radian a second of turn at a full cruise, capped 0.7), and rides its wings: the wings'
  height above their own mean (read from the pose, the roots named in `wings`) lifts the body as they sweep down
  (`heave` px per radian, 50 ms behind). A flier keeps all of its stroke climbing or hovering, glides down a dive
  (`glide`, the stroke's share kept, about the wings' mean), and at a cruise beats and glides by turns on a slow wave of
  its own (about six seconds). A body whose clips only glide (the owl's `air`) gets the layer's own beat (`flap`: radians,
  cycles a second, the tips' trailing share): down in 40% of the cycle, up in 60%, quicker climbing and hovering (x1.15,
  +0.4 per radian of climb), slower in a cruise (-0.35); the tips (`tips`) trail it by an eighth of a beat. The spine
  (`spine`, the links behind the body, front first) carries its swim stroke stronger with speed (`wave`: the stroke's
  scale at rest and at a full cruise, about each link's mean) and curves into a turn (`bend`, radians over the whole
  spine per radian a second, the tail to the inside of the turn); fins (`fins`) fold back at speed (`tuck`); the head
  holds level against the pitch and bank (`level`). Hand-built bodies beat on the life layer's paced clock (the moth's
  wings, the ray's ripple, the serpent's wave), so a change of pace never jumps the phase.
  The **Hollow Owl** beats 0.7 rad at 2.4 a second (tips 0.5) round its glide pose, heave 2, glide 0.12, banks 0.18,
  climb 0.6. In the air its body lies forward along the line of flight (75° off its upright stance, a 2° rock), and a
  cube-less `yoke` at the shoulders turns back by as much under the head and wings: the face still looks ahead, the wings
  still spread level and beat up and down about the line of flight (a wing hung from a pitched body would row); the legs
  trail under the tail, which fans straight back. Before this it flew upright, a perched owl hung in the air; the **Bogwick** (clip beat) heave 0.6, glide 0.6, tilt 0.25; the **Empress Moth** (its clip heaves) glide
  0.45, bank 0.16; the **Plumed Coil** wings heave 0.8, glide 0.4, spine of ten bending 0.25, wave 0.7/1.2; the **Dune
  Wyrm** spine of nine bending 0.3, climb 0.7, wave 0.7/1.25; the **Glimmerfin** tail and caudal fin wave 0.55/1.3, bend
  0.3, pectorals tucking 0.6, climb 0.7; the **Lantern Maw** wave 0.6/1.2, bend 0.25, bank 0.12; the **Tidesteed** tail
  and fluke wave 0.6/1.3, bend 0.25; the **Brook Otter** swimming, tail wave 0.6/1.3, bend 0.3; the **Lumen Moth** and
  **Petalwing** heave 0.9, glide 0.7 and 0.4, tilt 0.3 and 0.25, bank 0.25; the **Dune Ray** heave 0.8, bank 0.3, its
  tail bending 0.35; the eels (**Deep Eel**, **Tide Eel**, **Cord-Eater**) bend 0.45 over six segments, climb 0.6.
  The Breathbell's bell pulses as its clip has it (a jelly drifts; no bank or pitch).
- Test: `creature_motion_feet` (every motion.json entry with a gait names a rig; every gait finds two-bone legs on a body bone that
  carries the head; every foot can reach its stance on its crouch and sunk to stalk; the IK lands each foot within 0.05 px of its
  home, a step ahead and behind, the top of a step's arc and the crouch, checked by forward kinematics; the hip's turn
  survives its ZYX Euler angles; a straight leg whose knee can't hide 20° of bend is rigid (the four-legged walkers all
  are, so no knee of theirs breaks either way), and a rigid leg's foot lands within 0.05 px of each spot within 97% of
  its length with its top kept inside the body (no further fore, aft or down than its room, no more than 70% of its
  length up); at least 68 rigid legs; every gait's stride, walking and running,
  sweeps its planted feet no further than the hips can vault to; every gait's feet, on flat ground through a stand, a
  sudden walk (a cycle a second), a sudden run and a stop, never plant further ahead of home than a steady stride's
  landing plus 10% of a stride or trail further than its lift point plus 40%, and a rigid leg never swings past 35°
  walking or 45° running (about its pivot `shoulder` above the hip); then turned on the spot at 120° a second as a
  client sees it (the body held until its facing is 50° ahead, then dragged along 50° behind, the body bone twisted its
  share of that look), no planted foot is more than four `settle`s (+1 px) off its spot under the twisted body nor a
  rigid leg past 25°, and stood 1.5 s after it every foot is back within a `settle` (+0.75 px) (the old feet failed 22
  gaits); the forms' rigs
  are looked up too); `creature_motion_flight` (every flight names a creature and, on a rig, bones it has, wings with a
  side; the beat sweeps down in under half a cycle and never jumps; a right turn banks right and curves the spine right;
  a climb noses up and keeps every beat, a dive noses down and glides, a hover beats, a cruise glides between beats; a
  climb beats faster than a cruise; the body rises as the wings sweep below their mean). Tours walk still (NoAI) creatures with
  `/awaken admin stroll <targets> <blocks per tick> <ticks> [degrees per tick] [climb, blocks per tick]` (each call queues a leg; the server moves
  them every tick, so a busy runner can't turn a scripted walk into a crawl the way a tp a command did), load the studio's
  chunks first (`forceload`) and fill its floor twice. Tours on CI (PACK=perf,feel; a vanilla spider under
  Fresh Animations beside each): `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-lurker.txt` (clips run-autopilot/clips/lurk_*: idle, a walk
  into a run, a stop and a turn, a blow, a death, the hunt), `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-spiders.txt` (spid_*: the forms'
  row from vanilla's rungs to S, a walk side by side, a blow, a death, a hunt) and `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-crawlers.txt`
  (crawl_*: the thousandfoot, wickling, hushling and weaver queen); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-fliers.txt` (fly_*, swim_*:
  each flier on a set course, NoGravity, beside a parrot, a bee or a cod under Fresh Animations: a cruise, a U-turn
  each way, a climb, a dive, a hover; a blow and a death in the air; the swimmers in a tank);
  `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-close.txt` (close_*: each grazer and the spider side on at leg height, a spectator camera
  gliding beside it, first vanilla's under Fresh Animations then ours at rung 3 on the same walk, trot, stop and half
  turn; then the two at rest side by side for half a minute); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-beastclose.txt` (bclose_*:
  the sow, the stag and the ram the same way, after vanilla's pig under Fresh Animations, each then half a minute at
  rest); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-flyclose.txt` (fly_*, swim_*
  close and at half speed (`/tick rate 10`): each flier hovers, then circles a spectator camera at its own distance, a
  cruise lap and half a slower one, the camera's eye at the body's middle turning with it from the circle's middle,
  a parrot, a bee or a cod a little further round the same circle). A NoAI fauna creature refreshes its pose
  bits every tick (`FaunaMob.tick`), so a tour's still flier shows itself aloft (the first fliers tour's owls hung
  upright in the air, perched).

## 24. Hands: the first-person system (plan docs/anims/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/5dQodY76zUGpn536Z34Lpy; approved 2026-10-25)

Euan: "right now for basically everything there is no first-person animation". One owner for everything drawn in first
person, as the Feel Director is for the camera (module `anims`; public face `core.api.FirstPerson`; built in phases P1-P6
of the plan). No mixins.
- **World layer**: your body in first person, posed in the world (`anims.client.WorldBody`): a `WorldPose` source fills a
  `FirstPerson.Rig` (each limb from its root toward its tip, its front, a weight; `Rig.reach` slides a rigid limb's root
  so its fist or foot lands on a spot); the highest priority source that poses this frame wins (movement 100,
  interactions 200, combat 300). Limbs are parts of a private copy of the player model (vanilla's own is posed by every
  player in the frame and drawn after submission), with your skin, sleeves and pants. Legs are drawn in the world with
  real depth (`SubmitCustomGeometryEvent`). Arms are viewmodels (P1 tour: a fist a third of a block from the eye filled
  half the frame): drawn in the hand pass, each fist where the world puts it on screen but at 0.85 from the eye, the arm
  rising to it from under the frame's corner on its side (view (±0.5, -0.85, -0.1)); vanilla's hands step aside. No
  torso (from inside the head it is only a slab under the camera). Never in third person. Like vanilla's hands, none of
  it shows with the HUD hidden (F1).
- **View layer** (`anims.client.Hands`, the one owner of `RenderHandEvent`, first for each hand and last for the off
  hand): every `ViewPose` stance adds moves (view space: x right, y up, z toward you, blocks; then pitch, yaw, roll in
  degrees) for both hands, the main or the off hand; the body's stances (sprint, slide, hang, mantle) and the rope's
  arm moved here from their own hand listeners. The casts (powers) still draw their own arms until P3.
- **View clips**: `assets/awaken/fp_clips/*.json` (`anims.FpClipSet`, schemaVersion 1) written by
  `tools/art/specs/fp_moves.py` (edit there; `preview DIR` draws vanilla's arms from the eye); keys in ticks eased by
  `anims.Ease` (the same curve names as the third-person clips), authored right-handed and mirrored for a left main arm;
  a one-shot ends at rest; `FirstPerson.play(name[, speed])`, `stop` (a 3-tick fade), `playing`; keyed events reach
  `FirstPerson.listen` listeners (sounds, hit-stops). Combat's animations use the same three layers.
- **Fists** (P2): a view clip (`"fists": true`) or a stance may key where each EMPTY hand is on screen (view space)
  instead of moving vanilla's arm by offsets: its arm is drawn rising to the fist from under the frame's corner (from
  view (±0.48, -0.84, -0.53), vanilla's own arm start), so a hand can be lifted anywhere without its forearm floating into
  view (offsets that lift a vanilla arm show its end: the P2 preview). Vanilla's resting fist is
  `FirstPerson.View.REST_FIST` (0.744, -0.455, -1.072); a clip's fists replace a stance's for that hand; a hand holding
  an item ignores fists (vanilla draws it) unless a cast or a climb puts the item away (below). A fist clip gives the hands back at rest (or the off hand out under the
  frame), or, marked `toStance`, where its stance holds them (the hang's ledge jumps).
- **Grips** (Arms 2026-10-26, Euan: "it feels like the weapon is just floating and attacking on its own"): a source may
  key where a hand that HOLDS something closes on it (`View.gripMain`/`gripOff`, view space, weighted as fists): that
  hand's arm is drawn rising to the grip from under the frame's corner exactly as a fist's (after the moves for both
  hands, so it sways with what it holds), and the held thing still draws (a grip never hides the hand). Unset (weight 0)
  nothing changes. Arms keys them every frame a styled weapon is held: at rest, through each swing's turn, the guard
  and the equip rise, the off hand's on a pair's twin. Test `arms_grip`.
- **Put away** (Euan 2026-10-27: "climbing while a weapon is out doesn't hide the weapon, so it looks really weird"):
  whenever the hands grip the world, what they hold goes out of view and the fists take its place. Asked by a cast clip
  (`View.stow`, `"stow"`: at once, as before), by a climb (`View.climb`: the hang and its shimmy and every move between
  holds while `RunnerMoves.hanging()`, a wall climb, the Ascent's rope, zip line and rappel; and the clips marked
  `"climb"` in fp_moves.py: `fp_grab`, `fp_lower`, `fp_ledge_up`, `fp_ledge_side_l/_r`, `fp_mantle` (every mantle and
  climb out, a fence or wall climbed onto), `fp_rope_fire`), and on each side the world layer has an arm (the pipe's
  grip, a crossing's planted hand, the slide's trailing hand, a hard landing's palms). Each hand eases separately
  (`Hands.STOW`): going away it sinks 0.6 down the view (vanilla's equip drop) over 2.5 ticks (smoothstep; its grip arm
  sinks with it) while that hand's fist comes up into place from 0.8 under it, then is hidden; once nothing asks, it rises
  back over 3 ticks while the hand's last fist sinks 0.8 away (a world arm lets go in the world instead). A pair's twin
  goes with the off hand. Letting go of the lip (a drop, `fp_ledge_back`, a wall jump), the rope (`fp_rope_release`,
  `fp_rope_launch`) or the line brings the weapon back at once; a climb out keeps it away to the end of `fp_mantle`. The
  tactical sprint, slide (its main hand), roll, wall-run, vault and hop keep it in hand.
  Third person (2026-10-28): both held items, including a pair's twin, are hidden during a ledge hang and moves between
  holds, pipe/ladder grip, vertical wall climb, mantle/climb out, climbs over or onto rails (`HIGH`, `ONTO`, `OVER`),
  and the Ascent's rope, zip and rappel. `body.client.BodyHeldItems` clears only the extracted hand meshes and stacks,
  after Arms has populated them; the player's equipment never changes. The next extraction restores current equipment
  as soon as climbing ends, including after an interrupted mantle or climb-out.
  Dimension/respawn reset first ends tactical sprint, slide and vault through their normal cleanup paths, so removing
  transient movement state cannot strand a sprint speed modifier or forced crawl pose. The local player uses movement
  prediction; observers use the server's current transient `body_stowed` Boolean attachment (updated only on change,
  after movement validation, and sent on initial tracking too). It works without the animation library. A climb-out's
  server window is the same 10 ticks as its path plus the existing 6-tick Runner grace, ended sooner by the client's
  completion/interruption; other windows retain their existing motion limits. Death/replacement, logout and dimension
  changes retain no stow state. No save schema changes. Tests: `body_climb_stow` (state, ends, isolation, resets) and
  `tools/tests/body-held-items.py` (actual modifier, both hands, paired-item appearance, prediction and next-frame restoration).
- **Look-lag** (P2): the hands trail fast turns of the view on a damped spring (up to 0.06 sideways, 0.045 up, 4° of
  roll), halved with reduced motion (`FirstPerson.reducedMotion`, the body's setting).
- **Near legs** (P2): a foot nearer the eye than 1.15 is drawn in the hand pass, pushed out along its line of sight to
  that distance, as the arms are; farther legs stay in the world. (No source puts one there since P2.1 cut the slide's
  legs: from eyes 0.4 up they could only be a slab across the frame.)
- **Clean fists** (P1.1; Euan, 2026-10-25): the hands are vanilla's own blocky fists, never modelled fingers (finger
  boxes read as loose bricks). A world arm rises to its fist from under it on its own side (its root follows the fist
  across by `WorldBody.RISE` 0.45), not from the frame's corner, so a hand high in the frame never drags its sleeve
  across it. A world rig sets `handDistance` (nearer reads bigger: touches 0.75, both hands 0.85, stations 0.8, the
  pipe 0.85, the slide and landing 0.78), `held[]` (an item at the fist: a plucked flower, food being laid) and `glow`.
  Vanilla's hand steps aside only on the side the world body has an arm (a touch with one hand leaves the sword in the
  other); what it holds sinks away first (§24 "Put away"). In the hand pass the frame shows y down to about 0.7·|z|: keep keyed fists inside it.
- **The Runner's Kit in first person** (P2, `body.client.BodyFp`): each move's view clip starts from the same event as
  its third-person clip (BodyAnims hands the clip's name over): `fp_roll`, `fp_mantle` (and every climb out),
  `fp_grab`, `fp_lower`, `fp_ledge_up`, `fp_ledge_side_l/_r`, `fp_ledge_back`, `fp_walljump_l/_r` (the run's wall side),
  `fp_vault` and `fp_leap` (the free-run), `fp_slide_jump`, `fp_land_soft` / `fp_land_hard` (a fall over 0.55 b/t,
  hard over 0.95; never over a roll), `fp_stair_bump` (each half step a stair slide passes). Stances: the tactical
  sprint's lowered hands pumping in step (empty fists pumping up into the lower frame in turn, P2.1), the slide's brace, a
  wall-run's wall-side fist at the frame's edge brushing the wall with each footfall, a wall climb's fists slapping up in
  turn, a hang's fists on the lip (`BodyFp.HANG_*`, swaying; shimmying hand over hand). The wall jump's shove is well
  in the frame. World (source `body_moves`, 90; P2.1): the slide's trailing hand (the off side) on the
  ground where the eye's ray through view (±0.42, -0.34) meets it (the step under it on stairs), skimming it with a
  friction shake; a hard landing's fists slapped onto the ground under view (±0.2, -0.3) (down 3 ticks, held to 7, back
  by 12) instead of `fp_land_hard`;
  feet to the wall in a hang. No legs in a slide. The stair slide tips the view 9° down the run (`BodyCamera`).
- **The Ascent in first person** (P3, `body.ascent.client.AscentFp`): moments, each where the Ascent gives the Feel
  Director its beat: `fp_rope_fire` (the main arm flings the rope), `fp_rope_release`, `fp_rope_launch`, `fp_wings_open`,
  `fp_wing_beat` (every beat, the one that takes flight too), `fp_barrel_roll`, `fp_boom` (hands up against it),
  `fp_double_jump`, `fp_air_dash` (the lead fist punches through), `fp_dive` and `fp_slam_land` (fists up for a dive slam
  or the Judgement Fall, smashed down on landing), `fp_sovereign_ascend`. Stances: on a rope the main fist holds it at
  view (0.3, -0.02, -0.72), where AscentRender now starts the rope in first person, the other hand joining to pump
  (forward) and climbing over it to reel (sneak); a zip, both hands on it; flying free, arms out low for balance (fists
  up in a dive slam); wings, arms out flat at the frame's edges trembling with speed (swept out of the frame folding into
  a dive); flight, one fist forward on a boost, palms down in a hover, arms sweeping up to climb, swept back cruising; in
  the Sovereign's form the arms are tinted gold (`FirstPerson.View.tint`).
- **Reaches** (P4.1, `anims.client.Reaches`, world source `anims_touch`, 200): a touch's hand goes to the thing and does
  it there. Each touch is a few keys (tick, s across, u up, n out toward you) about where the hand meets the thing (its
  anchor, followed as it moves: a creature's flank, a lid's edge), from and back to rest under the frame's foot,
  smoothstepped; drawn at 0.75 (both hands 0.85). A door's palm meets it where you clicked (vanilla's door is open by
  then) and pushes on through. The player never moves (Euan, 2026-10-25: walking you to the thing
  would take control): past 2.5 blocks the hand only gets an arm's length (1.3) toward the thing, and while a hand is out
  the view narrows ×0.95 (a lean; off with reduced motion). A chest's screen waits 4 ticks for both hands to reach its
  lid (the menu is already open; the server is never held). The fist clips below stay for books (no world thing).
- **Touches** (P4, `anims.client.Touches`, `anims.AnimsClips`): quick hand moments from the game's own interaction
  events (client side), so every module's blocks get them by what they are: a door, trapdoor or gate (`DoorBlock`,
  `TrapDoorBlock`, `FenceGateBlock`) pushed with a palm (`fp_push`), a lever thrown (`fp_lever`), a button pressed
  (`fp_button`), a chest, barrel, ender chest or shulker box's lid lifted with both hands (`fp_lid`; the screen opens at
  once and covers it in single player), berries or a plant that breaks at a touch (no hardness, no collision: flowers,
  ferns, grass, the Living Wilds' herbs) pinched and plucked (`fp_pluck`), an animal stroked with an empty hand
  (`fp_pet`), a meal from a bowl held up with the free hand under it (a stance while eating); P5 adds the Forge (block
  id `awaken:forge`, not its class) or an anvil hammered three times (`fp_hammer`, 18 ticks: holding the blade being
  tempered, the off hand strikes) and food a campfire takes (`RecipePropertySet.CAMPFIRE_INPUT`) laid on it by the hand
  holding it (`fp_lay`). P6 adds: a palm pressed to a stone and held while the light answers (`fp_palm`, 18 ticks; the
  hand lit from within, `View.glow`, and cooled a touch, 5-18) on Awaken's waystone, conduit, ascent stone, Hearth anchor,
  rest and Stillpoint shrines, gate entrance, seal and rune (by id) and vanilla's lodestone, respawn anchor and beacon; a
  notice torn off the Spire board (`fp_tear`); a grindstone cranked (`fp_crank`); a page turned at a lectern, an
  enchanting table, or as a book or the Dream Journal opens (`fp_page`); the smithing table hammered (`fp_hammer`); both
  hands set to a stonecutter, loom, cartography table or brewing stand (`fp_set`, two-handed like the lid); any
  `awaken:*_cache` lifted like a chest. The Ritual of the Bell (`story.client.RitualFp`, a view stance): kneeling in the
  bow both palms go flat to the floor (eased in over 6 ticks), as the eyes open the main hand comes up against the bloom
  (50-132), at the End both hands rise palms out, shaking harder as the light drains (30-195), and drop at the error. At most 9 ticks each; the
  action never waits; a swing cuts them; with the main hand full the off hand does it (each has an `_off` twin), with both
  full nothing. Settings (feel): `firstPersonMoves` (P1-P3) and `firstPersonTouches` (P4), both on.
- **Station scenes** (P5, `anims.client.station`): at a crafting table (used within 10 ticks of its screen opening, not
  sneaking: sneak + use is the plain screen) the screen is replaced by `StationScreen` (kind `TABLE`), the vanilla
  crafting menu with its grid and result drawn on the table in the world instead of on the screen. Each
  ingredient lies flat, centred on its drawn square (the texture's: 2-pixel squares a square every 3 pixels, middles on
  pixels 5, 8 and 11 of 16, so `CELL` = 3/16 and the grid 9/16 across; row 0 the far one; the way in snapped to an
  axis; a flat item 0.16 across, a block half that), the result lies flat on the top's near border (0.41 in from the
  middle toward you, 0.17 across, turning slowly where it lies), inside the table's own block so it never reaches into a
  wall, and flat it never hides a square (it once floated over the far edge and went into the wall behind; over the
  middle it hid the far middle square), the square under the cursor (and every square a drag has passed over,
  showing what it will get) is outlined (Holo blue).
  - **Layout** (`anims.station.StationView`, common so the tests run it headless): your inventory is a glass strip at
    the foot of the screen (vanilla's image, `top` = screen height - 165, the strip over its rows), the hint over it
    (wrapped to the room's width, centred), and above the hint the *room*: the middle half of the screen's width with
    JEI loaded (at least the strip's width), else the screen's width less 8 each side, from 6 px down to 4 px over the
    hint. The screen reports room and strip as its area (`getLeftPos`/`getTopPos`/`getImageWidth`/`getImageHeight`),
    so JEI's list and bookmarks keep to the sides. Hints: "Works just like a crafting grid. Sneak as you open it for the
    usual screen." and the furnace's.
  - **The view** frames the station: from your eye, the yaw, pitch and vertical field of view that fit every slot (a
    grid square ±3/32, the result ±0.085, a furnace's opening) inside the room, 6 % to spare, turned so they sit in its
    middle (`StationView.frame`, recomputed each tick; at most 100° or 1.5× your FOV setting). It eases in over 12 ticks
    (6 coming back within 12 s), out over 10; the player's own look never moves. Standing 1 to 4 blocks from a table at
    any GUI scale the framing stays under 100°; pressed right against it (under 1 block) the near edge can reach the hint.
  - **Clicks are vanilla's**: the scene screen is vanilla's own container screen, and a station slot is under the
    cursor where the world shows its square (`isHovering` answers from a ray through the view as drawn; the slots'
    old screen places are never hovered or drawn). So every mouse and key rule of the crafting grid holds: left click
    lays the held stack or takes it, right click lays one or takes half, left-drag splits evenly, right-drag lays one
    per square, double-click collects, shift-click on the result crafts all it can into the inventory and a plain click
    takes one craft, number keys, Q and the pick key work on the hovered square or slot, shift-click from the inventory
    moves into the grid; all through the menu's own clicks, which the server checks. Only a point inside the room picks
    a square: a click on the strip, the hint or a side panel never reaches the station. A click outside the room and
    the strip drops what you carry, as off any container screen. Your hands (world source `anims_station`, 200) rest off the table's near corners and one goes out to every
  square whose contents change (and to the result as it is taken), over 9 ticks; moving, jumping, E or Esc leave.
  A hand moves only within 6 ticks of your own click on a slot, so a furnace cooking on its own moves none; taking a
  result moves the hand to the result only.
  - **Furnaces** (kind `FURNACE`: vanilla furnace, smoker and blast furnace; Codex's furnace-interior, reviewed
    2026-10-28): the view drops to the mouth's height (block y + 0.57) where you stand; your body and your look are not
    moved. A client-only camera entity (StationCamera, unregistered, like the opening's OpeningCamera) carries the
    lowered view, eased in and out like the table (12/6 ticks in, 10 out); the field of view is set through the
    final-FOV hook, since a camera that is not the player gets no FOV-modifier event. The scene opens only from the
    front, 0.85 to 4.5 blocks from the block's middle, and only while the far item's edge still shows through the mouth
    (0.30 either side of it); from the side, the back, too close, or with something in the way you get the plain furnace
    screen. Eight rays 0.12 out from the eye's corners keep the drop from passing through a floor, wall or low ceiling;
    they are cast when the scene opens and again every tick (never every frame), so a block placed into the path while
    you work gives the view back and shuts the screen. Moving, jumping, E or Esc, another camera, death, a new level and
    logging out also give it back. Your own body is hidden from the lowered view; the hands rest beside it, by the
    shoulder (0.35 under the eye, clear of the floor), and only a working hand reaches into the frame.
  - **A real mouth:** every furnace, smoker and blast furnace in the world gets a block model with a recessed mouth
    (all four facings, lit and unlit): the five outer faces and a stone frame stay, the cavity is x 3–13, y 2–13, z 0–9
    model pixels with soot-dark walls and back (vanilla's cobbled deepslate, by name) and a coal bed, and a lit one glows at
    the back of the coals. The cavity's faces are lit from the air in front of the mouth (cullface north, so vanilla's
    block renderer reads the light there instead of inside the solid furnace, which is always 0; Sodium unchecked): an unlit furnace
    reads as a deep sooty hollow, not a black hole, and the cavity is culled when a solid block covers the front. Items sit
    3/16 inside the mouth at scale 0.24: what cooks on the left, the finished result on the right (±0.15, y + 0.57),
    the fuel on the coals (y + 0.26). They stay still while vanilla's flame, smoke and cooking go on. Each slot is
    picked within 0.16 of its middle and gets the front-facing outline; the cooking (Holo blue) and the fuel left (fire)
    still run as two thin lines over the strip; fuel is the off hand's, the rest the main hand's. The hint reads "Cook on
    the left, add fuel below, and take finished items on the right. Sneak as you open it for the usual screen."
  - **What's inside, screen shut:** the server sends each player read-only copies of the three slots of nearby
    furnaces (FurnaceContents, payload `furnace_contents`): the nearest 64 within 16 blocks, found every 40 ticks in the
    nine loaded chunks around them (`getChunkNow`, never a load), compared every 5 ticks, and only changes and
    removals sent. Using a furnace sends its contents at once, before the menu opens. Leaving range, an unloaded chunk,
    a replaced block, a new dimension and logging out drop a view; coming back reads it fresh. Nothing is saved and
    nothing in the furnace is changed. The items are drawn only within 16 blocks and from in front of the mouth, depth
    tested behind the opaque cavity walls (never through a wall); everyone nearby sees them whatever their
    `stationScenes` setting, which only turns the scene on or off. Recipes, fuel, taking items, XP and saves stay
    vanilla's. (A hacked client could read the contents of a furnace behind a wall within 16 blocks; a furnace shows
    its contents openly anyway, so this is accepted.)
  - **Other mods and packs:** no mixins. Only a plain single-variant cube furnace model is replaced; a resource pack's
    or mod's non-cube or wrapped model is left alone, and then the furnace has no scene and no items in its mouth (the
    plain screen opens). A mod that gives furnaces their own block-entity renderer keeps its look the same way. The
    models use vanilla's own textures by name; no Mojang file is copied. Setting `stationScenes` (feel), on.
- **The lens** (P5): the hand pass draws at a fixed 70°; anything the world anchors (arms on a pipe, at a table; near
  legs) has its view x and y scaled by tan(35°) / tan(world FOV / 2), so it lands where the world shows it on screen even
  with the view narrowed or widened (a station's zoom, the speed FOV). The lowered furnace camera uses the actual HUD
  FOV from the render state for that ratio, because its final-FOV hook affects both projections.
- Test: `anims_fp_clips` (the file reads, every clip the body and the touches play is in it, every one-shot gives the
  hands back). The table scene: `anims_station_frame` (seven GUI sizes from 320×240 to 1280×720, with and without JEI,
  standing 1 to 4 blocks off each side: every slot lies inside the room and a click on its middle picks it),
  `anims_station_cells` (each way in: every ingredient on a drawn square's middle, row 0 far, the result on the near
  border, all inside the table's block, a click straight down picks each),
  `anims_station_panel_click` (a square under the strip while leaning in: a click there picks nothing), and the clicks
  vanilla's screen sends on a real crafting menu: `anims_station_right_click`, `_right_drag`, `_left_drag`,
  `_shift_result`. Furnace regressions: `anims_furnace_camera_pick` covers all four facings, high/low player eyes,
  approach distances/offsets, small and large GUI layouts, all slot picks, and wall/near-plane collision rejection;
  `anims_furnace_contents` uses real vanilla smelting and save/reload, two viewers, inventory mutation, range/rejoin
  and removal; `anims_furnace_recess_geometry` checks the six packaged models have an open mouth and opaque backing.
  These are headless checks; rendered appearance, camera feel and third-party renderer combinations need in-game
  verification. Tours: `tools/autopilot/anims-pipe.txt` (P1), `anims-runner.txt` (P2), `anims-ascent.txt` (P3),
  `anims-touch.txt` (P4: filmed with the pilot's clip recorder, since a command reaches the client a few ticks late),
  `anims-station.txt` (P5), PACK=feel, HUD on. Pilot lines `use`, `attack`, `usehold <ticks>` press the real keys;
  `station <slot> [button]` clicks a slot of the open station scene.
- P1-P6 built (P5: the crafting table and furnace scenes, the Forge and campfire touches; P6: the rest of the touches, books, the Ritual's hands). Tour P6: `anims-p6.txt`. The casts (powers) still draw their own first-person
  arms (`CastAnims`); folding them into Hands is the powers module's step, coordinated with the combat plan.
